title: 第一盘太酸了  (Batch One Is Too Sour)

segments.t: In the café corner, the first cake cools on a wire rack. Manager Zhou measures out the lemon glaze while his reading glasses sit forgotten on his forehead, and Chen wanders over for a bite. Listen first.
第一盘柠檬蛋糕烤好了——让我用大勺子浇糖霜！
周经理，您又把老花镜推到头顶上啦，能看清刻度吗？
没问题！这瓶黄色的肯定是甜柠檬糖浆，倒进碗里就行。
大厨，烤箱里飘出来的杏仁味儿把我从院子里馋过来啦。
老陈来得正好！一号盘的柠檬脆皮蛋糕刚切开，快尝一小块！
我特意多浇了两勺糖霜，保证香甜又柔软。
那我就不客气啦，先咬一大口……哎哟我的天哪！
老陈，您的脸怎么皱成了一团？不好吃吗？
这蛋糕酸得连我手里的黄铜指南针都能擦亮啦！
什么？我赶紧把老花镜戴上……哎呀，这瓶是纯柠檬浓缩汁！
周经理，难怪糖霜看起来那么稀——您忘了放糖！
留着吧，下次谁要洗石头喷泉，就给谁吃第一盘！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
第一盘柠檬蛋糕烤好了——让我用大勺子浇糖霜！

'The first lemon cake is done baking—let me pour the glaze using the big spoon!' "Kao hao" pairs "bake" with "good" to mean successfully finished, and "jiao" is the action of pouring liquid over something.
周经理，您又把老花镜推到头顶上啦，能看清刻度吗？

'Manager Zhou, you have pushed your reading glasses up onto your head again; can you read the markings clearly?' "Laohuajing" names glasses for "old-flower" (farsighted) eyes, and "kan qing" joins "look" and "clear".
没问题！这瓶黄色的肯定是甜柠檬糖浆，倒进碗里就行。

'No problem! This yellow bottle is definitely sweet lemon syrup; pouring it into the bowl is fine.' "Ping" is the counter for bottles, and "daojin" pairs "pour" with "enter" as the liquid hits the bowl.
大厨，烤箱里飘出来的杏仁味儿把我从院子里馋过来啦。

'Chef, the almond aroma floating out from the oven tempted me over from the courtyard.' "Piao chulai" paints the scent "drifting out", while "chan guolai" means Chen's appetite playfully "gluttoned" him over.
老陈来得正好！一号盘的柠檬脆皮蛋糕刚切开，快尝一小块！

'Chen arrives at the perfect time! The lemon crisp-crust cake in Tin One was just sliced open, hurry and taste a small piece!' "Zhenghao" captures "exactly right" timing, and "kuai" counts chunky pieces like slices of cake.
我特意多浇了两勺糖霜，保证香甜又柔软。
'I specially poured two extra spoons of glaze to guarantee it is fragrant, sweet, and soft.' "Teyi" marks Zhou doing something "specially" on purpose, and "duo jiao" means "pour more".
那我就不客气啦，先咬一大口……哎哟我的天哪！

'Then I will not be polite; I will take a big bite first... oh my goodness!' Polite guests say "bu keqi" ("not acting like a guest") before digging in, and "yao yi da kou" gives "bite one big mouthful".
老陈，您的脸怎么皱成了一团？不好吃吗？
'Chen, why is your face scrunched up into a ball? Is it not delicious?' "zhou cheng yi tuan" paints his sour expression literally wrinkling up into a tight "ball" (tuan).
这蛋糕酸得连我手里的黄铜指南针都能擦亮啦！
'This cake is so sour it could polish the brass compass in my hand until it shines!' "Lian... dou..." wraps the compass to say "even it could", and "ca liang" joins "rub" with "bright".
什么？我赶紧把老花镜戴上……哎呀，这瓶是纯柠檬浓缩汁！

'What? I will hurry and put my reading glasses on... oh dear, this bottle is pure lemon concentrate!' "Dai shang" uses "dai" for wearing accessories like glasses, and "aiya" slips out when Zhou realizes his mistake.
周经理，难怪糖霜看起来那么稀——您忘了放糖！
'Manager Zhou, no wonder the glaze looks so thin—you forgot to add sugar!' "Nanguai" dawns on Mei as "no wonder / hard to blame", and "fang" means "put in / add" for ingredients.
留着吧，下次谁要洗石头喷泉，就给谁吃第一盘！
'Keep it; next time whoever needs to wash the stone fountain gets to eat Tin One!' "Liu zhe" means "keep it staying", and "shui... jiu gei shui" pairs "whoever" with "then give whoever".

Chen drinks a full glass of water while Zhou sheepishly wipes his reading glasses. One mysterious recipe line remains! See you next time.
